short: Recognizer-to-lip-reader distillation (M02) is ahead of the prior record and repeats over two datasets and three teachers; the audio rationale is untested and the LRS2 state-of-the-art claim fails.
position: The paper [@zhao2020hearing] changes the training-only supervision (M02): a speech recognizer is distilled into a sentence-level lip reader at three granularities, transcripts kept, which the authors call "the first attempt along this line" (§1). Before 2019-05, audio entered training of 76 sentence-level lip-reading and audio-visual decoders as forced-alignment targets (12, 8 for the visual stream) and never as distilled teacher outputs (0, pattern match, Appendix); the closest prior, Li et al. (2019-04) [@li2019crossmodal], distils into an audio-visual student. For a video-only student the design is ahead at the time, shared with the [concurrent] Afouras et al. [@afouras2020asr]. The gain repeats on CMLR, LRS2 and all three teachers, single values without run counts (§4), but the rationale that the benefit comes from audio is untested: a [later] same-student comparison finds a video teacher about as useful [@ren2021master]. The state-of-the-art claim (M12) holds for CMLR only; on LRS2 the paper's Table 5 lists two earlier systems with lower WER.
